cases.input: A Python analyzer emits unused-redefinition diagnostics between class methods decorated with module-imported typing.overload; inspection finds immediate-scope-only lookup.
Public typing.overload declarations with another decorator emit unused-redefinition diagnostics; inspection finds an exactly-one-decorator requirement.
Repeated functions use a decorator named overload, but its binding identity and diagnostic owner are unknown.
Two ordinary undecorated functions share a name and receive an unused-redefinition warning.
A runtime multiple-dispatch library chooses the wrong function implementation without any static unused-redefinition diagnostic.
